title: Serve a small language model
brief: Build a tokeniser, a KV-cached generator, a sampler, speculative decoding, and LoRA merging around a given tiny transformer, and prove each stage matches the slow, obvious version.
hints: decode_step is forward for one row: take the position from cache.length before appending, append the new key and value, then attend over everything the cache returns. Compare with forward(params, tokens)[-1] after every token.

In speculative_round, the draft's rows give q and the target's rows give p. On a rejection, draw the replacement from max(p - q, 0) renormalised, never from p, or the output stops following the target.
merge_adapter must return a copy. Use copy.deepcopy(params) and replace only the adapted weights; alpha / r multiplies B @ A, not alpha alone.
